html:
A Japanese painter and printmaker of Edo, the master of the ukiyo-e woodblock print. His Great Wave off Kanagawa is one of the best known images in the world.

He worked for some seventy years and used dozens of names. He made book illustrations, paintings, erotic prints and thousands of sketches, published in many volumes as the Hokusai Manga.

Around 1830, past seventy, he made his series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. It used the new imported pigment Prussian blue and turned the landscape into a main subject of prints, which had mostly shown actors and beauties. He also made print series of waterfalls, bridges and the Tōkaidō road.

He said he hoped to keep improving until he was over a hundred. When Japan opened to the West in the 1850s and 1860s, his prints reached Europe and fed the craze called Japonisme. Painters such as Monet, Degas and Van Gogh studied his work, and it shaped Impressionism.
